Sexually active; last intercourse ~4 days ago. Contraceptive implant in place ~1 year; menses irregular on implant; LMP ~2–3 weeks ago. No prior pregnancies.  
- Relevant family medical history:  Not recorded.

- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings:  23-year-old with acute, constant, worsening suprapubic pain and light vaginal spotting; mild nausea; slight vaginal discharge; sexually active; implant in situ; LMP ~2–3 weeks ago; last pregnancy test 1 month ago. No fever, syncope, dyspnea, shoulder pain, or urinary dysuria.  
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx and transcript):  
  - Ectopic pregnancy: Moderate likelihood. Pain + spotting; no pregnancy test since symptom onset; implant reduces but does not eliminate pregnancy risk. Needs urgent exclusion.  
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID): Moderate likelihood. Pelvic pain with abnormal bleeding and slight discharge in sexually active patient; absence of fever does not exclude.  
  - Functional ovarian cyst (including hemorrhagic/ruptured cyst): Moderate likelihood. Acute pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting; implant users can have functional cysts.  
  - Acute appendicitis: Low–moderate likelihood given worsening pain and nausea, though location and lack of systemic features are less typical.  
- Working diagnosis:  Acute pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting — etiology undifferentiated. Priority is to rule out pregnancy/ectopic and assess for PID or ovarian pathology via in-person evaluation.  

Management Plan

- Actions and recommendations:  
  - Arrange urgent face-to-face clinic assessment for abdominal/pelvic examination (patient agreed to call support line to book).  
  - Perform a pregnancy test today. If positive, seek immediate medical review (call back urgently).  
  - Safety-net advice: If pain worsens significantly, unable to keep fluids down, or any concerning symptoms (e.g., dizziness, fainting), seek urgent care before scheduled appointment.  
- Follow-up:  Face-to-face appointment to be arranged by patient via support line.  
- Patient education:  Discussed need to rule out pregnancy/ectopic and importance of in-person exam for further diagnosis.  

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

- Ectopic pregnancy — Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: Pelvic pain and light vaginal bleeding; sexually active; no pregnancy test since symptom onset; implant lowers but does not eliminate risk.  
- Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) — Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: Lower abdominal pain with abnormal bleeding and slight discharge in a sexually active patient; afebrile does not exclude PID.  
- Functional ovarian cyst (including hemorrhagic/ruptured cyst) — Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: Acute pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting; possible association with contraceptive implant.  

Quality checks

- Missing expected elements: Vital signs (BP, pulse), full abdominal/pelvic exam, urinalysis, pregnancy test result, STI risk assessment and screening, cervical screening status, immunization review, BMI/weight, alcohol and smoking history, mental health screening, hearing/vision screening.  
- Internal contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx. Some history elements unclear (e.g., alcohol/smoking not clarified).  
- Transcript quality: Audio/communication intermittently unclear; several responses incomplete or ambiguous; limited data due to teleconsultation without examination.
